standard_prerequisites: formal spectra and rig-surjectivity tested on adic maps to complete discrete valuation rings
the faithfully-flat case of the preceding rig-surjectivity lemma
vanishing of I-torsion versus I-power torsion and the Noetherian annihilator lemma
the Jacobson lemma on primes defining closed points of the complement of a closed point
embedding of a one-dimensional local domain into a discrete valuation ring and faithful flatness of maps of rings detected on spectra
core_obligations: Prove that under vanishing I-torsion and flat finite-type reductions, Spf(B) to Spf(A) is rig-surjective iff A/I to B/IB is faithfully flat
proof_roadmap: Faithful flatness implies rig-surjectivity by the preceding lemma

Conversely, pick a maximal ideal m of A containing I; vanishing of the I-power torsion makes U = Spec(A_m) minus V(I) nonempty and the Jacobson lemma gives a prime q of A_m outside V(I) defining a closed point of the punctured spectrum
A_m/q is a one-dimensional local domain embedding into a discrete valuation ring R with IR inside the maximal ideal, so A to R extends continuously to the completion R^wedge
Rig-surjectivity supplies the lift to B, hence a prime of B over m; this for every m shows Spec(B/IB) surjects onto Spec(A/I), which for flat A/I to B/IB is faithful flatness
difficulty_reason: H2: a lift-construction converse; the source writes the reduction to a one-dimensional quotient and the final surjectivity-to-faithful-flatness step.
